Keywords: Parchment scraping and iron gall ink
RagShortTexts: Parchment requires dehairing, stretching, scraping and smoothing.
Writing, ink and binding add to a book’s cost.

Variants.Content: Parchment is dehaired, stretched, scraped and smoothed before ruling and writing. Skins, ink and scribal labor determine the book’s price. Holes or mistakes require writing around them, repair or replacement.
Traveling documents need protection against water and abrasion. If damaged writing obscures an order, its bearer must seek clarification rather than guess essential names or amounts.
A charter costs more than its skin: literate witnesses and custody matter. Clear names, boundaries and a known place of keeping let the document support a disputed agreement.
Scribes economize on costly skins, but deep scraping weakens a sheet. Workshops need light, ink and binding arrangements; haste can waste an entire written skin.
